title: IBM and Microsoft Launch Imagine Enterprise Agent Platform
summary: IBM and Microsoft unveiled Imagine Enterprise on Nov 10, 2026, seeding the agent platform with 6,000 pre-built agents for finance, insurance, retail.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- IBM and Microsoft launched Imagine Enterprise on November 10, 2026, with 6,000 pre-built IBM Consulting agents.
- First industry frameworks target financial services, insurance, and retail with governance controls for regulated sectors.
- SEI, managing $2 trillion in assets, is the named early customer for the joint platform.


IBM and Microsoft unveiled Imagine Enterprise on November 10, 2026, seeding the joint agentic platform with more than 6,000 pre-built agents and assets from IBM Consulting. The platform targets regulated industries with governance controls designed to log agent actions and enforce autonomy limits, addressing compliance demands in financial services, insurance, and retail.


Officially launched on November 10, 2026, Imagine Enterprise integrates IBM Consulting Advantage tooling with Microsoft Foundry, GitHub Copilot, Copilot Studio, Fabric, Microsoft 365, Entra, Purview, Defender, and Azure. SEI, which manages approximately $2 trillion in assets as of September 30, 2026, is the named early customer.


## Platform Architecture and Integration


Imagine Enterprise combines IBM Consulting Advantage, including Process Studio, Context Studio, and Advantage Core, with Microsoft's full enterprise AI stack. The architecture positions IBM's 6,000 pre-built agents as industry-specific modules that run on Microsoft infrastructure. The vendors frame the governance layer as controls, observability, and AI-compliance support aimed at regulated industries, though the launch announcement does not detail how individual agent actions are logged for auditors.


The platform ships with first frameworks for financial services, insurance, and retail. IBM named manufacturing, energy, public sector, and mobility as next targets but did not disclose delivery timelines for those frameworks.


## Early Customer and Use Case


SEI is the sole customer named in the launch announcement. Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next, said the firm is applying AI with intention to strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making, and create value across the business. The asset manager's participation signals demand for agent platforms in wealth management and advisory workflows, where regulatory oversight and audit trails are table stakes.


The vendors did not disclose additional pilot customers or pricing details for Imagine Enterprise. No public roadmap for expanded industry frameworks has been published.


## Positioning in the Enterprise Agent Market


IBM and Microsoft position Imagine Enterprise as a response to enterprise buyers who want agentic automation, not productivity tooling. Mohamad Ali, senior vice president and head of IBM Consulting, said clients are no longer looking for AI that helps people do the same work a little faster; they want to build an agentic business. Rodrigo Kede Lima, president of the Microsoft Frontier Company, framed the win condition as turning data, industry expertise, and AI into action.


The launch lands in a crowded enterprise-agent week. Google Cloud rolled out Gemini for Healthcare the same day, and OpenAI introduced verified business profiles in ChatGPT earlier in the week. The timing reflects intensifying competition for enterprise agent deployments as vendors race to ship industry-specific frameworks before year-end.


## What This Means


Imagine Enterprise is a statement play in the enterprise agent market, combining IBM's consulting depth with Microsoft's infrastructure footprint. The 6,000 pre-built agents give enterprise buyers a faster path to production than custom-built agent workflows, but the success of the platform will hinge on governance tooling, audit transparency, and the pace at which IBM and Microsoft ship additional industry frameworks. SEI's participation validates demand in regulated sectors, but broader adoption will depend on pricing, deployment complexity, and the willingness of enterprises to trust joint-vendor platforms for mission-critical workflows.
